findings: Headphones, earbuds and accessories carry a median discount of 63%, ranking 2 of 13 sub-categories with at least 15 listings (highest: WearableTechnology at 75%, lowest: OfficePaperProducts at 10%).

62% of headphone listings are discounted by 60% or more, against 37% elsewhere in Electronics. A deep discount here is the norm and largely reflects a high listed MRP, so the discount percentage is a weak signal on its own.
Among brands with at least 3 listings, Zebronics has the lowest median selling price (₹449) and Noise the highest (₹1,299). Boult discounts deepest at a median of 78%.

Across 63 headphone listings the rank correlation between discount depth and number of ratings is -0.23 (95% bootstrap CI -0.45 to -0.01). The interval excludes zero, but this is an association within one snapshot, not evidence that discounts cause demand.

Across all 1,349 products the same correlation is -0.13 (CI -0.18 to -0.08): more heavily discounted listings tend to have fewer ratings, which is consistent with discounts being used on less popular items rather than discounts driving popularity.
